goal: Make deleting a user a soft delete that keeps the record but hides it from listings

requirements.summary: Implement soft deletion for user records by marking them as deleted without physically removing them from the database.

requirements.description: The `UserService` should provide a method to mark a user as deleted.
When a user is soft-deleted, their `deletedAt` field should be set to the current timestamp.

acceptanceCriteria: Calling the delete method on the UserService for a specific user updates their `deletedAt` field.
The deleted user's record remains in the database but is not returned by any listing queries.
constraints: Soft deletion should only be applied to users, not other entities like posts or comments.
assumptions: The `UserService` has access to the necessary database operations and fields.
openQuestions: How should soft-deleted users be excluded from listing queries?
outOfScope: Updating UI or notifications for deleted users

plan.objective: Implement soft deletion for user records by marking them as deleted without physically removing them from the database.
plan.scope: This plan focuses on modifying src/services/userService.ts and src/routes/users.ts to support soft deletion. No UI or notifications are updated, in line with out-of-scope requirements.
assumptions: The `UserService` has access to the necessary database operations and fields.

tasks.title: Add soft delete functionality to UserService
tasks.description: Modify the `UserService` to support marking users as deleted by setting their `deletedAt` field.
tasks.rationale: The existing `deleteUser` method only removes records, which does not satisfy the requirement for soft deletion. Adding a new method will allow us to mark users as deleted without removing them from the database.

files.change: Add `softDeleteUser` and update `deleteUser` to mark users as deleted.

tests: src/services/userService.ts: should update the user's deletedAt field when softDeleting a user
tests/userService.test.ts: should test that softDeleted users are not returned by listUsers
acceptanceCriteria: Calling the `softDeleteUser` method on the UserService for a specific user updates their `deletedAt` field.
The deleted user's record remains in the database but is not returned by any listing queries.

tasks.title: Update usersRouter to use soft delete
tasks.description: Modify the `usersRouter` to call the new `softDeleteUser` method from UserService.
tasks.rationale: The existing `deleteUser` endpoint only removes records, which does not satisfy the requirement for soft deletion. Updating this endpoint will ensure that soft deletion is used instead.

files.change: Replace `deleteUser` with `softDeleteUser` in the delete route.

tests: src/routes/users.ts: should test that softDeleted users are not returned by listUsers
acceptanceCriteria: The `usersRouter` uses the new `softDeleteUser` method from UserService.

risks.description: Potential bugs in the implementation of `softDeleteUser` could lead to incorrect soft deletion.
risks.mitigation: Thoroughly test the `softDeleteUser` method and its integration with other parts of the application.

risks.description: The existing tests might not cover all edge cases for soft deletion, leading to potential regressions.
risks.mitigation: Review and update existing tests to ensure they cover all relevant scenarios.

openQuestions: How should soft-deleted users be excluded from listing queries?

rounds.summary: The plan effectively implements soft deletion for user records by modifying the `UserService` and updating the `usersRouter`. The scope is appropriate, and all tasks are well-defined with clear dependencies.
